title: Role-Based Access Control — Operator, Reviewer, and Admin Roles
goal: Add a three-tier role model so organizations can give consultants scan access, clients read-only review access, and administrators full system control, without everyone having the same permissions.
scope: Builds on backlog-120 (API key authentication must be complete first). Add role enforcement to the api_keys table from backlog-120. Three roles: admin (full access including settings and user management), operator (can create runs, approve, view findings, generate reports — cannot change global settings or delete engagements), reviewer (read-only: can view findings, reports, download reports — cannot create runs, approve, or change any data). Enforce roles on sensitive endpoints: POST /runs requires operator or admin, POST /runs/{id}/dispatch requires operator or admin, DELETE /runs requires admin, PATCH /settings requires admin, POST /findings/{id}/evidence/verify available to all. In Settings, add a Users section showing API keys with their roles, last used date, and revoke button. Add Create API Key form with name and role selector. In the topbar actor pill, show a role badge next to the actor name. Role is stored in the api_keys table from backlog-120.
generation_reason: All actors currently have identical permissions. Enterprise clients need to share reports with stakeholders without giving them scan access. Consultants need scan access without admin rights.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Three roles only (admin/operator/reviewer). No per-engagement roles in this slice. Requires backlog-120 to be complete.

success_criteria: Three roles defined: admin, operator, reviewer.
Operator cannot call DELETE /runs or PATCH /settings (403).
Settings shows Users section with API key management.
Tests cover role enforcement on key endpoints.

acceptance_criteria: Role enforcement works on sensitive endpoints. User management in Settings.
